column2: A starling murmuration at winter dusk. HUE: ember amber (~25 deg), from a deep burnt-umber dark to a pale peach glow. The glass is the sky over a reed bed: the sky in dithered bands of the one hue, brightest at the horizon where the sun has just gone, the reeds, a line of poplars and a pylon or two as flat silhouettes in the darkest shade. The time IS the flock: a couple of thousand starlings (1-2 px dark specks at sub-pixel positions, a few bigger near ones) whose density draws the numerals: design a set of ten 'flock numerals' with swelling ribbon strokes, dense cores, feathered tendril edges and clean open counters, so the flock reads first as birds and then, unmistakably, as the time. Constant life from the flock's own physics: density waves roll through it, the dark 'black wave' of birds banking passes along a numeral, edges ripple and stream, stragglers catch up, a few birds peel away and rejoin. Minute turn, the centrepiece: the changing digit's birds peel off in a river, loop through the sky in one long ribbon and pour into the new numeral's shape (old shape fully dissolved before :00, the new one condensing after it), a continuous flow, no teleporting; the other digits keep wheeling. Hour: a bigger show, e.g. a peregrine falcon (bold flat silhouette) stoops through the flock: it bursts into a vortex and a hole tears open, then the flock re-forms the time; the time stays readable throughout. Night: the sky falls to the dark end of the hue, a pale moon disc, and the birds must still read (perhaps the flock becomes the light thing on the dark, or settles onto wires and reeds as the time).

A handheld game cartridge from the 1989 four-shade era. HUE: the old pea-green LCD (~80 deg): exactly four shades of ONE green from near-black olive to pale lime, as the original handheld had, plus that screen's ghosting and its slightly visible pixel grid. Not a copy of any real game or character: invent a little platformer with its own hero (a bold 16x16 sprite with a clear silhouette, big eyes, readable at --scale 4) and its own tileset (8x8 tiles: bricks, question blocks, pipes, ladders, coins, springs). The time IS the level: the four numerals are built from the game's tiles as level geometry the hero runs over, climbs and jumps between (design all ten digits as tile-built platforms with clean counters, edges and caps drawn as proper tiles, not a font made of squares), with a HUD line in the game's own 8x8 tile font (score, coins, world, lives) that is clearly secondary. Constant life: the hero plays the level every second (runs, jumps with a proper arc, collects coins, bops a little enemy), parallax hills and clouds scroll at different line rates behind, coins spin, water or lava tiles cycle. Pixel art moves in whole pixels: at 60 fps keep it at most ~1 px per frame so it reads smooth. Minute turn: the hero smashes the old digit's blocks from below (bricks burst into the classic four spinning fragments, gone before :00), then the new digit's blocks pop up after :00 one by one with a bump, or rise out of pipes. Hour: a bigger show, e.g. a level-clear (flagpole or goal, fireworks, a score tally) and a screen wipe into a new world tileset (forest, desert, ice, castle, all in the same four greens), the time readable throughout. Night: the game's own night level.

Chinese paper-cutting (jianzhi), the red window flower. HUE: cinnabar red (~355 deg), from a deep oxblood to a pale pink of light coming through rice paper. The glass is a lattice window at the new year: the backlit rice paper is the pale end of the ramp, the paper-cut is flat red, and its cut holes glow pink where the light comes through. The numerals are cut from one sheet of red paper and obey the craft's rules: everything is connected (a paper-cut must hold together as one piece), strokes carry the cutter's own vocabulary (crescent moon cuts, sawtooth zigzag edges, teardrop and comma holes, little fishscale and swirl cuts, ribbon ends), and each digit is designed as a cut figure with its counters open and its silhouette unmistakable, framed by flowers, fish, lanterns, clouds or a cockerel of the year in the same red. Constant life: a breeze makes the paper sway and bow gently on its tape (a flat ripple, not 3D), the light behind shifts and glows through the cuts, petals or snow drift past outside as soft shadows, a small hanging tassel swings. Minute turn, the centrepiece: a pair of scissors (bold flat silhouette) cuts: the old digit is snipped out piece by piece and the scraps flutter down (gone before :00), and after :00 the scissors cut the new numeral along its path, the cut-out bits falling away to reveal it. Hour: a bigger show, e.g. a folded square of red paper is cut and then unfolds (accordion and radial folds opening one after another) into a symmetrical medallion that frames the new hour, the time readable throughout. Night: lamplight inside, the window glows deeper.

Chladni figures: sand singing on a vibrating plate. HUE: cobalt blue (~215 deg), from a near-black blue-violet plate to a pale ice-white sand. The glass is a dark metal plate, bowed at one edge by a violin bow or driven by a small speaker at its centre (both flat silhouettes in the ramp), and covered in fine pale sand that gathers on the plate's nodal lines. The numerals are nodal figures: design a set of ten digits whose strokes are the flowing, symmetric curves of standing-wave patterns (the ornamental quality of real Chladni figures: curves meeting in crosses, lenses and rings), so they read first as sand ridges on a singing plate and then, unmistakably, as the time, counters open. Constant life: the plate hums: grains at the antinodes hop and glitter (single bright pixels popping up and falling back), sand creeps along the lines toward the ridges, a faint shimmer of the vibrating surface, the bow moves to and fro. Minute turn, the centrepiece: the tone glides to a new frequency: the old digit's sand leaps into a dancing cloud and scatters (old figure gone before :00), and after :00 it drifts, bounces and settles onto the new figure's nodal lines, the new digit condensing out of the noise: the fluent physical motion of sand. Hour: a bigger show, e.g. the plate sweeps up through its harmonics: the whole plate (except the time's own digits, which stay readable) flows through a series of classic Chladni mandalas before landing on the new hour. Night: the plate darkens to the deep end of the hue and the sand glows faintly.
